newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka oil refinery resumes operation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka oil refinery resumes operation.

text.p: Sri Lanka's only oil refinery, run by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), has resumed operations after an unscheduled 11-day shutdown, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
"We commenced operations yesterday (Tuesday). The refinery is processing crude now," a senior CPC official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.

The 50-60,000 barrels per day capacity refinery was shut down on May 30 because of insufficient crude after the CPC's single point mooring buoy (SPMB), which discharges crude from tankers to the refinery, was damaged in an accident.

CPC officials earlier said a previously scheduled reopening had to be pushed back because the refinery had not received enough crude as a 60,000-tonne tanker was discharging at a slower rate due to a problem with the tanker.
"That tanker has finished discharging and the refinery has enough crude to begin processing," the official said.
Another tanker carrying 85,000 tonnes of crude will begin discharging on Wednesday through the SPMB, he said.
CPC has a crude oil storage capacity of 150,000 tonnes.
